summary.intent: Get a natural-sounding, live voice-conversation phone alert for the ask-soony hackathon demo (agent calls the buyer, answers questions, records an approve/escalate/reject decision), ideally using GPT-Realtime or ElevenLabs, while keeping costs and compliance hurdles low.
summary.outcome: Upgraded Twilio, bought a US number, set up an ElevenLabs agent (gpt-4.1-mini with Claude Haiku backup), and built an OpenAI Realtime SIP provider with webhook, handover script and decision function. Calls initially failed as 'busy' due to the user's Do Not Disturb; later GPT-Realtime calls connected, and turn detection and noise handling were being tuned, with background noise still a problem and no confirmed end-to-end decision recorded yet.

repo: Call providers sit behind one interface selected by ASK_CALL_PROVIDER (openai or elevenlabs); the escalation logic and dashboard are shared.
Secrets and the user's address live in the gitignored .env (TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, ELEVENLABS ids, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_PROJECT_ID, OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET, ASK_ADDR_*), and are never printed in chat.
The dashboard is exposed through a tunnel at ask-soony.stenglein.dev; the OpenAI webhook endpoint /hooks/openai rejects unsigned requests with 401.
The record_decision tool posts to the dashboard webhook with a per-alert secret token that the model never sees.
Main files touched: src/ask_soony/openai_calls.py (new), dashboard.py, escalation.py, tests/test_alerts.py, plus pyproject.toml/uv.lock for the websockets dependency.
workflow: Check the real state through APIs (Twilio usage records, pricing API, ElevenLabs agent listing) instead of estimating.
Background tasks that wait for call end and print logs/transcripts were useful for diagnosing calls.
Add logging of model/user turns and OpenAI errors to diagnose failing realtime calls; it revealed the model cancelling its own speech five times due to line-noise turn detection.
Multi-step scripts that fall back automatically (German number, then US number) can spend money without confirmation; ask before purchases.
OpenAI webhook event types differ between organization and project settings pages: realtime.call.incoming appears only on the project page.
Twilio does not offer German or Belgian numbers to individuals without a local address or business bundle; US local numbers need only the account KYC.

friction: Twilio refused number purchases until KYC in Trust Hub was approved.
The script bought a US number automatically after the German purchase failed, without asking the user first.
German local/mobile numbers need a business bundle, and the console failed with 'Regulation not found'; the Belgian number needs a Belgian address, so the US number stayed.
The first calls reported 'busy' because of the user's Do Not Disturb; the cause was only found after several failed attempts.
The user's project ID was pasted onto the OPENAI_REALTIME_VOICE line and had to be moved.
The user saw only safety events in the OpenAI webhook dialog because they were on the organization page, which cost several rounds of diagnosis.
GPT-Realtime calls had the model cancel its own speech because of noisy turn detection; background noise at the user's location persisted after tuning.
US-number calls to German mobiles cost $0.3763/min versus about $0.042/min from EEA numbers.
open_items: Confirm a full GPT-Realtime call end to end (greeting, Q&A, record_decision on the dashboard); noise handling was still being tuned.
Possibly enable interruption again once noise handling is solid (currently disabled on purpose).
Open question whether GPT-Live SIP support is enabled for the OpenAI project.
Option to switch to a cheaper EEA number (e.g. Belgian mobile) later, if a local address and approved ID bundle become available.
Release the US number after the hackathon to stop the $1.15/month fee; keep auto-recharge off.
Build a PWA with push notifications and in-app voice conversation as a free everyday channel.
Alert #4 is still open with no decision from the earlier failed ElevenLabs call; the ElevenLabs agent stays as a fallback and has not been test-called successfully.
Fallback of GPT-Realtime over Twilio Media Streams (own audio relay) if SIP does not work.
